item: Wikipedia, ORES and DuckDuckGo sessions refuse a redirect to a host outside their list, on every hop
key_paths: src/safety/fetcher.py; src/wiki/client.py; src/wiki/ores.py; src/services/duckduckgo.py; tests/test_session_host_list.py; docs/SECURITY.md
summary: The parked LOW from the sink sweep: the three clients followed any redirect from their fixed endpoints with no host check and no connect-time SSRF guard. requests calls Session.send for the first request and again for every hop, and GuardedSession only overrode request, so the kill switch and transport choice ran once and nothing ran on a hop. GuardedSession now takes an optional allowed_hosts and checks the whole URL in send, before every request: EthicalFetcher._refuse_parser_mismatch (backslash, whitespace or control in the authority, any percent in the host, the two parsers disagreeing, non-IDNA hosts), then https only, no userinfo, port 443 only, and a listed host (an exact host, or a leading-dot suffix meaning any host under it, never the bare domain or an empty label). A refusal is RedirectRefused, a RequestException and not a ConnectionError, raised before the request is sent, naming the clause and never the address. Lists: the wiki client wikimedia.org + .wikimedia.org + .wikipedia.org (its one shared session also serves pageviews on the bare apex and EventStreams), ORES .wikimedia.org, DuckDuckGo duckduckgo.com + .duckduckgo.com. The sessions that redirect between CDNs by design (dumps, OSM, segmented download, installer, statistics, catalog and entity loaders) stay unlisted and are pinned in UNLISTED_SESSIONS with zero slack, so a new one is a decision. Tests: each refusal clause has a test only it can fail, and a mutation matrix over the check left no survivor. Not covered, and said so: the unlisted sessions; no connect-time SSRF scope (the hosts are fixed public ones). Ruff advisory 417 of 417.
